properties.statement: `describe_schema`'s HINT FOR `CAUSES.validation_status` NAMES FOUR VALUES, AND THE ENUM ACCEPTS FOUR DIFFERENT ONES. Found here, in this repo, on 2026-08-08, by following describe_schema and being refused. The hint reads: 'Whether the causal claim has been tested (observational / intervention / mechanism / temporal).' The enum is `["unvalidated", "hypothesis", "validated", "refuted"]`. NOT ONE OF THE FOUR WORDS IN THE PROSE IS ACCEPTED. I called describe_schema BEFORE writing the edge — which is what AGENTS.md says to do instead of guessing — read the parenthetical as the value list, and the write was refused. THE REFUSAL WAS EXCELLENT and is why this is minor: it named the edge, the property, the offered value and all four accepted ones, so the fix took one retry and no investigation. The cost is one round trip; the significance is the class. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE brainstorm/add_decision DRIFT REPORTED BY dev_storyflow THE SAME DAY, one layer lower: two halves of the SAME served surface, shipped from the SAME binary, disagreeing about that binary's behaviour — there a skill against a tool, here a property's description against its own validator. And it is the more troubling instance of the two, because a description sitting beside the enum it describes has NOTHING between them: no build step, no separate file, no drift window. Whatever guard dec:idea-a-skill-may-assert-the-defaults-it-relies-on settles on for skills, a description and its enum living in one struct ought to be checkable mechanically and is not. FIX SHAPE: correct the hint to the accepted values; and consider a lint that fails when a property description contains a parenthesised slash-separated list whose members are not the property's enum values — crude, but it would have caught this one and it is the pattern every such hint uses. NOTE THE HONEST BOUND ON MY OWN CLAIM: I did not audit the other property descriptions. This is one instance found by tripping over it, not a survey, and the survey is the obvious next step.
